name: The Socialite
note: Address shown by search results: 79 Jefferson St (permit listed 77 Jefferson St), Fisherman's Wharf

facts.text: A brewpub that brews its own beer on site at its Fisherman's Wharf location.
The Fisherman's Wharf location was previously home to Fire & Brew.
Its original location is on Brannan Street.
Opened in 1966 by George Matson and Alexis Muir.
Run as a collectively owned queer bar since 2016, under The Stud Collective.
Closed in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic and reopened in 2024 at this location.
Reopened in 2021 under new owners after about 10 months of renovations.
A neighborhood bar in the lower Nob Hill area.
Hosts a pub quiz every Monday night.
Serves weekend brunch with bottomless mimosas.
Hosts live jazz.
An Irish pub that also hosts live music, trivia and bingo.
Occupies a 1916 Beaux Arts space that was formerly home to the original Standard Oil Company.
A sherry-focused bar with about 30 sherries by the glass.
Has a multi-level back patio with picnic tables and TVs on each level.
A sports bar with U-shaped booths facing large TVs.
A heated, covered outdoor dining space open year-round.
Owned and operated by Hi Neighbor Hospitality Group, which also runs The Vault Steakhouse.
Sits on the 39th floor of the San Francisco Marriott Marquis.
Its signature martini, the Ten/89, is named after the hotel's opening story.

name: The Wooden Nickel
note: Yelp title lists 1900 Folsom St as CLOSED; SFGate article (sfgate.com/food/article/wooden-nickel-sf-bar-closed-17882649.php) reports it will not reopen after flood damage

name: Thee Parkside
note: SF Examiner and SF Chronicle report it served its last pint July 5 after 26 years; building at 1600 17th St sold to a developer

facts.text: Founded by Chef Phil West and bartender Jeff Lyon, who worked together at Range.
A cocktail bar that also makes its own jerky, some smoked and some vegetarian.
Occupies two levels with three bars in about 10,000 square feet.
Its food menu is made in partnership with Stag Dining Group.
The signature drink is the Fire Bowl, a blended rum, vodka and gin punch served in a volcano tiki bowl.
The site at 4146 18th Street was formerly home to The Pendulum bar.
The building's facade was restored in 2008 for the filming of Milk.
An LGBTQ dance and video bar with a patio.
Formerly named Gather Dogpatch, under the same team.
Pours low-intervention wines, many certified organic or biodynamic.
Its lagoon was built from the Fairmont's Terrace Plunge swimming pool, installed in 1929.
MGM set director Mel Melvin was hired to convert the pool into the Tonga Room.
Simulated rainstorms with thunder and lightning fall over the lagoon.

name: Tonic
note: Hoodline reports Tonic closed its Polk and Union location in April 2018 and moved to Lower Nob Hill; address tonicbar-sf.com/OSM is stale

facts.text: Opened as Tony Nicco's Cafe right after Prohibition ended in 1933, in a building that had housed Madame Nicco's French Laundry.
Charles 'Butch' Lavagnino bought it in 1951 and renamed it Tony Nik's.
Sold in 2000 to owners including Tony Nicco's grandson.

name: Top of the Mark
note: Address null; lounge is atop the InterContinental Mark Hopkins

facts.text: Hotel owner George D. Smith converted the Mark Hopkins penthouse on the 19th floor into a glass-walled cocktail lounge.
The name came from friends' reply when Smith said he did not know what to call the top of The Mark.

name: Tope
note: Yelp title: TOPE - CLOSED, 1326 Grant Ave; Updated June 2026

facts.text: Owned by Dave Keene.
Pours from 50 taps and three cask handpulls.
Holds an annual barleywine festival.
A tiki bar that opened in 1937.
Has been run by the same family for over 30 years.
Founded by Josh Harris of Bon Vivants Hospitality.
Changes its cocktail menu theme each season, including zodiac signs and neighborhood-themed drinks.
From bar director Nicolas Torres and chef David Barzelay, the team behind Lazy Bear.
Makes drinks with California ingredients such as pinecone distillate and redwood tips.
